text.p: The St Louis Cardinals added some speed to the lineup Wednesday when they signed second baseman Delino DeShields, who had been with the Los Angeles Dodgers, to a one-year contract with a club option for a second season. Financial terms were not disclosed.

The 28-year-old DeShields, who was third in the National League will 48 stolen bases, batted .224 with five homers and 41 runs batted in for the Dodgers last season. He has a career .263 average with 301 stolen bases.
DeShields was somewhat of a disappointment during his three seasons in Los Angeles after coming to the Dodgers from the Montreal Expos in 1994 for pitcher Pedro Martinez.
DeShields did not hit over .256 in any campaign for Los Angeles, after batting .289 or better in three of his four years in Montreal.
Regarded as a weak defensive second baseman, DeShields has also struck out more than 100 times in a season in three different years, including 124 whiffs in 1996.
"Delino is the prototypical leadoff man; someone who will bring additional speed and excitement to our team," said Cardinals' vice president and general manager Walt Jocketty.

"In the long run, we felt that Delino gave us our best option, because we didn't have to mortgage our future by trading away prospects and we still have some flexibility to make additional moves to improve the team for 1997."
DeShields replaces veterans Mike Gallego and Luis Alicia, who shared the job last season.
